title: Hearing aid fitting
what: A specialist tests your hearing, chooses a hearing aid, and sets it up for your ears. The aid makes sounds louder and speech clearer.
why: When your hearing is reduced and speech is hard to follow, especially in noise or on the phone.
duration: the first visit usually takes 1 to 1.5 hours; getting used to it and fine-tuning takes a few weeks
tell_doctor: Any ear discharge, pain, or ear surgery
Ringing in the ears or dizziness
If your hearing dropped suddenly over a few days, see an ENT doctor urgently first
Where hearing is hardest for you: at home, at work, on the phone

prepare.title: Ears
prepare.text: An ENT doctor usually checks your ears first and removes any earwax plug.

prepare.title: Hearing test
prepare.text: If you have a recent hearing test, bring it. If not, it will be done on site.

prepare.title: Someone with you
prepare.text: It helps to bring someone close to you. Their voice can be used during setup.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
Your glasses, if you wear them
steps: The specialist asks where you have trouble hearing
Your hearing is tested with headphones: you press a button when you hear a tone
The type of aid is chosen: behind the ear or in the ear
Sometimes an ear impression is taken for an earpiece
The aid is connected to a computer and tuned to your hearing
You learn to put it in, take it out, and change batteries or charge it
feel: The hearing test does not hurt
At first, sounds seem loud and sharp, and your own voice sounds strange
You may feel the aid in your ear for the first days
after: Wear the aid every day, starting with a few hours
Getting used to it usually takes 2 to 4 weeks
Come back for fine-tuning. It is a normal part of fitting
Keep it away from water, and take it out at night
red_flags: Pain, redness, or discharge from the ear: take the aid out and see a doctor

faq.q: Do I need to wear it all the time?
faq.a: Yes, it is best to wear it all day. Your brain adjusts faster and understands speech better.

faq.q: Do I need aids for both ears?
faq.a: If hearing is reduced on both sides, two are usually advised. It makes speech easier to follow and sounds easier to locate.
Your brain has forgotten many sounds. This passes in a few weeks, and the aid can be adjusted if needed.

reminders.text: Hearing aid fitting tomorrow. Bring past hearing tests and, if you can, someone close to you.
